conviction_note: Baseline has no options and n=0 reactions, so I built my own anchor: the 15-Jun-2026 Q2 print (EPS beat, revenue miss) took the stock from 10.92 to 10.31, about -5.6%, so this name moves 5-8% on a miss, not the 1.83% deadband; my central case is revenue of roughly $7.0m against a published FY2026 consensus that requires $7.55m per quarter in H2, with EPS again in line to slightly better, which is the Q2 pattern repeated into a stock that has not repriced at all (20d run-up -1.18%) and whose covering analyst raised his target two days after the Q2 miss.

findings.finding: The published FY2026 revenue consensus of $28.72m requires H2 revenue of $15.11m (~$7.55m per quarter) against an H1 actual of $13.61m (~$6.81m per quarter), and the Marine Technology segment that has to deliver it printed $2.71m and $2.84m in Q1 and Q2 FY26 against a $4.0m year-ago Q3 comp — it would need a 14-18% sequential jump to a segment already running -19% for the half.
findings.why_not_priced: If this were priced the FY2026 number would have been cut after Q2's 8% revenue miss and the covering analyst would have cut his target; instead Freedom Capital Markets RAISED its price target from $13 to $14 on 2026-06-17, two days after the miss, and the target still sits 39% above the $10.09 spot. The stock is also flat over 20 days (-1.18%) going into the print, so nothing has been marked down in anticipation. A priced version of this looks like a stock drifting down into the event on cut numbers, not one sitting still under an unrevised consensus.
findings.independence: The segment run-rates are read directly off the company's own Q2 FY2026 10-Q (Marine Technology $2,839,592 vs $3,878,090; six months $5,549,256 vs $6,854,876) at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1334325/000149315226028609/form10-q.htm (filed 2026-06-15), and the $4.0m Q3 FY25 comp from the year-ago release at https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/09/15/3149838/0/en/Coda-Octopus-Group-Reports-Fiscal-Third-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results.html — three separate documents. NOTE: this finding shares the Q2 10-Q with finding 4 (inventory); treat that document as one source cluster.

findings.finding: The Middle East/Asia softness management called on 15 June 'not structural, it is a timing issue' that would 'resume swiftly' once pressure was alleviated instead escalated through the exact 1 May - 31 July fiscal Q3 window: the Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed to commercial traffic since 28 February 2026 and traffic slumped again in July on renewed US-Iran fighting and a blockade.
findings.why_not_priced: Hormuz itself is the most heavily covered macro story of 2026 and is obviously priced as a macro fact. What is not priced is the specific link to this issuer: CODA's UAE/Gulf offshore-survey customers are the named cause of the Q2 Products shortfall, management publicly assumed alleviation, and the consensus above was never revised for the fact that the quarter being reported sat entirely inside the closure and got worse in its final month. If the market had made that link, the FY2026 revenue line would not still imply an H2 acceleration and the stock would not be flat over 20 days.
findings.independence: Management's own 'timing issue... resume swiftly' framing and the UAE-projects-on-hold detail come from the Q2 FY2026 call transcript, https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/15/coda-octopus-coda-q2-2026-earnings-transcript/ (2026-06-15) — a different source from the shipping data. NOTE: that transcript is shared with findings 3 and 5.

findings.finding: Coda Octopus has issued zero order or contract-award press releases in the sixteen months since 13 May 2025, against a prior cadence of three in ten weeks (a $1.3m engineering order 26-Mar-2025, a $1.4m engineering order 24-Apr-2025, a $1.5m DAVD order 13-May-2025) — and every one of its seven 2026 releases is an earnings or earnings-call item — despite the CEO telling investors on 15 June that 'we expect to see some orders in our third quarter' for DAVD following the Approved-for-Navy-Use designation.
findings.source_date: 2026-09-11 (feed read today; the dated items cited are 2025-03-26, 2025-04-24, 2025-05-13 on page 2, and the 2026 items 2026-01-06 through 2026-08-24 on page 1)
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody aggregates the absence of a press release, and there is no data vendor field for 'order announcements not made'. If the market had priced a DAVD order failing to land, the Q2 call's single most-quoted forward statement would have been walked back somewhere in the coverage and the FY consensus cut; neither happened. Corroborated inside the Q2 10-Q, where customer concentration collapsed from three customers at 34.2% of H1 FY25 revenue to one customer at 10.2% of H1 FY26 — the large lumpy orders that generated those 2025 press releases have stopped arriving.
findings.independence: The CEO's Q3-order statement is from a different document, https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/15/coda-octopus-coda-q2-2026-earnings-transcript/ (2026-06-15). Caveat stated honestly: an IR policy change is an alternative explanation, and the Defense Engineering segment that produced two of the three 2025 order releases is growing +47% in H1 FY26 without any releases, which cuts against reading the silence too hard. Shares the transcript with findings 2 and 5.

findings.finding: Inventory stood at $13,995,256 at 30 April 2026, up 2.6% from 31 October, against quarterly cost of revenue of about $2.33m — roughly 1.5 years of COGS — while the Marine Technology segment that carries it fell 19% in the half; and a brand-new CFO, Mark Kelly, started 3 August 2026, after the quarter closed, on a three-month probationary period, and signs his first 10-Q with this print.
findings.source_date: 2026-07-06 (8-K, item 5.02; appointment effective 2026-08-03, succeeding an Interim CFO)
findings.why_not_priced: This is a conjunction nobody screens for: a first-time-signing CFO who arrived after quarter-end, replacing an interim, inheriting an inventory balance worth 1.5 years of cost of sales that is still growing into a shrinking high-margin segment. The 10-Q lands the same day as the release, so any reserve or obsolescence charge is disclosed simultaneously with the headline rather than a week later. If the market had focused on it there would be sell-side commentary on inventory turns or a CFO-transition note; CODA's coverage consists of one target-raise on 2026-06-17. Sized low as a mode because the modal outcome is that nothing happens, with a wide left tail.
findings.independence: The inventory, COGS and gross-profit figures are from the Q2 FY2026 10-Q, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1334325/000149315226028609/form10-q.htm (2026-06-15) — a different document from the 8-K. NOTE: that 10-Q is shared with finding 1; the scorer should collapse the two to one cluster.

findings.finding: Two-sided tail: the company disclosed on 15 June that it has 'two active opportunities that we are going through active due diligence on at the moment', holds $30.6m of cash and no debt (about 27% of the $10.09 spot in net cash) and has a $100m Form S-3 shelf that went effective 31 March 2026 with nothing drawn against it — so an acquisition or a raise could be announced alongside the print.
findings.why_not_priced: The brief correctly notes the shelf's existence is in the wire; what is not is that management has had two targets in active diligence for three months on a company whose organic high-margin segment is shrinking, and that the last such deal (Precision Acoustics) is the only reason FY2025 revenue grew 30.7%. The signed impact is positive but small because the shelf cuts the other way on a $111m market cap — a raise is the same event risk in reverse. If a deal were priced there would be a run-up rather than a 20-day drift of -1.18%.
findings.independence: The shelf is verifiable separately in EDGAR: S-3 filed 2026-03-19 and no 424B5 or prospectus supplement since, per https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001334325.json (retrieved 2026-09-11). Shares the transcript with findings 2 and 3.

searched_and_found_nothing: Form 4 / insider cluster: the only ownership filings in the run-in are a routine 1,102-share director award to Michael Hamilton (transaction 2026-05-28, filed 2026-06-24) and the new CFO's Form 3 showing zero shares (2026-08-04) — no insider buying or selling ahead of the print

The 10-K/A filed 2026-02-26 looked like a restatement lead and is not: it was filed solely to include the auditor's inadvertently omitted signature on the Frazier & Deeter report, with no other changes

The 8-K filed 2026-09-10, four days before the print, is a routine item 5.07 annual-meeting result — all seven directors elected, auditor ratified, say-on-pay passed; nothing extraordinary was put to shareholders (mild note only: Michael Hamilton drew 1.23m withheld votes, ~19%)
The $100m shelf effective 2026-03-31 has had nothing drawn against it — no 424B5 or prospectus supplement appears in EDGAR through 2026-09-11

US federal contract award databases (USAspending, HigherGov) for Coda Octopus Colmek: no readable FY2026 award records surfaced; the retrievable awards are from March 2025 and earlier, and the one '$906k defense contract' article that looked current is dated 2024-07-09
Company hiring/careers page, customer forums, app-store signals and distributor/channel chatter: not applicable or non-existent for a ~100-person B2B sonar and defence-electronics maker
No competitor, prime-contractor or supplier guidance issued after 15 June that names Coda Octopus or its Echoscope/DAVD product lines
baseline_tension: The baseline gives me no skew and no options to argue with and a 20-day run-up of essentially zero, so there is no priced directional statement to agree or disagree with — my findings cut against the one visible piece of positioning, a price target raised from $13 to $14 on 2026-06-17 against a $10.09 spot, and against the unrevised FY2026 consensus, while the honest counterweight is that the stock is already 39.8% off its high with 27% of its market cap in net cash, so the room to fall on a modest revenue miss is smaller than the arithmetic alone suggests.
